description: Documentation corpus for this service. One markdown file per surface or concept, in docs/. This index is what search_docs ranks over; read_doc returns a file's contents.

docs.title: Agents
docs.summary: An agent is a definition, not a process: a prompt, a set of tools, a model, and optionally memory. Running it produces a [run](sessions-and-runs.md).
headings: What an agent is made of

docs.title: Chat
docs.summary: The front door. Talk to any agent in the workspace directly; no node, no task, no setup.
headings: What you can point it at

docs.title: The CLI
docs.summary: `ah` drives the service from a terminal: the same operations as the dashboard, either in this process or over REST against a backend elsewhere.
headings: Two ways it reaches the service

docs.title: Connections
docs.summary: An agent that already runs in production, on its own triggers, reporting what it does into this hub. The hub starts nothing and only watches.
headings: When a graph stops to ask

docs.title: Connectors
docs.summary: Services this hub reaches out to: a Telegram bot, a GitHub or GitLab account, a local Blender install. The other direction from connections.

docs.title: Containers
docs.summary: Agents can run in-process or in Docker. Container mode isolates a run: its own filesystem view, its own network posture, its own lifetime.

docs.title: Costs
docs.summary: Token and estimated USD spend, broken down by workspace, agent, model or project, with budget caps that are enforced rather than advisory.

docs.title: Evals
docs.summary: Eval sets, graders and model sweeps: measure whether a prompt change helped instead of guessing.

docs.title: Flows
docs.summary: A flow is a graph of agents run as one pipeline: nodes do work, edges define order, and the whole thing streams as it goes.

docs.title: Imported agents
docs.summary: An agent that already exists, already works and has its own dependencies does not need rebuilding here. Import it from its git repository: the hub clones it, checks whether it can run, and adds it to the agent list either way.

docs.title: Installing and running the service
docs.summary: One command installs everything and puts `ah` on your PATH. The rest of the page is that command taken apart: by hand, in Docker, and what to check when it will not start.

docs.title: Instances
docs.summary: An instance is a live copy of an agent: its own state, its own label, its own history. Where an [agent](agents.md) is a definition and a [node](nodes.md) is a process, an instance is the thing actually doing work.

docs.title: Loops
docs.summary: A loop wraps a [flow](flows.md) and re-runs it, feeding back a reviewer's complaints, until an agent judges the result good enough.

docs.title: Marketplace
docs.summary: The catalog of agents, flows and skills published across workspaces: how a thing built in one workspace gets published, cloned and used in another.
headings: Publishing an agent, a flow or a skill
When to reach for a published agent

docs.title: Memory
docs.summary: Agents have five complementary memory layers, bound to a pool. The pool is assigned per workspace, so the same agent can carry different knowledge in different workspaces.

docs.title: Models
docs.summary: The Models page is the source of truth for which models exist, which are offered, what they cost, and which is default per provider.

docs.title: Nodes
docs.summary: A node is a long-running agent process. It polls for work and executes it, which is what lets a task run without a chat window open.

docs.title: What this service is
docs.summary: An agent hub: a place to define AI agents, give them tools and memory, and run them, alone or in groups, against real work in a workspace.

docs.title: Page chat
docs.summary: The button in the corner of every page: a chat about the page you are on, holding the records that page is showing.

docs.title: Playground: worlds and scenarios
docs.summary: The playground drops agents into a simulated world and runs it tick by tick, so you can watch behaviour rather than read about it.

docs.title: Projects
docs.summary: A project is one codebase or one effort inside a workspace. It gives work a folder, a structure graph and a task tree.
headings: What a project adds over a bare workspace

docs.title: Scheduling and the Plan page
docs.summary: Future work: notifications, agent tasks and flow triggers, plus the inbox showing what fired.

docs.title: Service health and diagnostics
docs.summary: Whether the moving parts are alive, and what to do when they are not.

docs.title: Sessions and runs
docs.summary: These two records are how everything in the product becomes observable.

docs.title: Settings
docs.summary: Credentials and connection details. What models are offered and which is default lives on the [models](models.md) page, not here.

docs.title: Skills
docs.summary: A skill is a reusable procedure an agent can follow: written once, surfaced when it is relevant to the task at hand.
headings: The part that trips everyone up

docs.title: System agents
docs.summary: An agent is either **system** (shipped with the product) or **custom** (yours). There is nothing in between.
headings: What being a system agent means
Why the last two are separate

docs.title: Tasks
docs.summary: A task is tracked work: it has a status, an owner, subtasks, dependencies, and a result that outlives the conversation that produced it.

docs.title: Teams
docs.summary: A team is a bounded roster of agents that know each other and work over a shared message board.

docs.title: Telegram
docs.summary: A Telegram bot can be bound to this service, so a conversation continues from a phone and notifications arrive where you are.

docs.title: Tools and capabilities
docs.summary: Tools are granted to an agent by name. Nothing is granted by default, including the calculator.
headings: Why capabilities and not tool names
Approval gates, which are a different thing

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.summary: Symptoms in the order people hit them: runs that will not start, output that never appears, numbers that look wrong, Docker, and the CLI.

docs.title: Views and Studio
docs.summary: A view is something an agent built to be looked at: a chart, a graph, a table, a 3D scene, a simulation, a slide deck or a document.

docs.title: Web requests
docs.summary: Every `web_search` and `fetch_url` call an agent made, recorded with the text it was actually handed. The **Web Requests** page is where you read them.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.summary: A workspace is the unit of isolation: its own folder on disk, its own roster of agents, its own settings, its own memory pools and its own projects.
